summary: Acornsoft, the software arm associated with Acorn Computers, ceased operating as a separate company after David Johnson-Davies left in January 1986. Afterward Acorn used the Acornsoft name on office software in the VIEW family for the BBC Master series. Superior Software licensed and rereleased many Acornsoft games from 1986, while Topologika handled most of the text adventure games.
one_line: Overview of Acornsoft's end in January 1986 and how its games and software were later published by Superior Software, Topologika and Acorn.
key_facts: Acornsoft ceased to operate as a separate company upon the departure of David Johnson-Davies in January 1986.
After this date, Acorn Computers used the Acornsoft name on office software it released in the "VIEW" family for the BBC Master series.
In 1986 Superior Software was granted a licence to publish some Acornsoft games.
Superior Software rereleased many Acornsoft games, both individually and as compilations.
Compilations rereleased by Superior Software include the "Play It Again Sam" series and the "Acornsoft Hits" series.
By agreement, the Acornsoft name was also used on the packaging of some of the subsequent Superior games.
Superior Software chose not to take on Acornsoft's text adventure games.
Most of Acornsoft's text adventure games were released in updated versions by Topologika.
Topologika also released some sequels to the text adventure games from the same authors.
